  "title": "How to compile and configure BoringSSL with nginx to support TLSv1.3",
  "body": "I saw a blog on your site showig that [Cloudflare is using BoringSSL](https://blog.cloudflare.com/make-ssl-boring-again/) and issue [#78](https://github.com/cloudflare/sslconfig/issues/78) also prove the usage of BoringSSL.\r\n\r\n>As it happens, BoringSSL has supported TLS 1.3 for quite a long time (it was one the first open source SSL implementations to work on this feature), so now all of our edge SSL traffic (including TLS 1.3 connections) is handled by the same system, with no duplication, no added complexity, and no increased latency. Yay!\r\n\r\nHowever I compiled BoringSSL with nginx 1.13.7  using configuration `--with-openssl=/path/to/boringssl --with-openssl-opt=enable-tls1_3` and it could not support TLSv1.3 Draft18 (like Cloudflare does).\r\n\r\nBoringSSL supported TLSv1.3 draft18 since [this commit](https://github.com/google/boringssl/commit/a833c357edae4eb7f47b9808bf744bd9bb0df18d) but I could not find an wiki or an explanation about how to compile and configure BoringSSL with nginx to support TLSv1.3 draft18.",

      "created_at": "2018-04-10T14:40:23Z",
      "updated_at": "2023-03-23T14:01:48Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "I was looking for the same solution and came across this post.\r\nBecause I have found a solution, it is neat to share it with you guys.\r\n\r\nI found this patch: https://l.avinz.nl/enabletls13boringssl\r\n\r\nIt will enable BoringSSL's TLS 1.3 draft 22 and 23 (Chrome stable) and the final TLS 1.3 standard (BoringSSL master only).\r\n\r\nIt is quite simple. \r\nAll you have to do is patch the BoringSSL chromium-stable or if you want BoringSSL master -code.\r\nCompile it against Nginx and you are done.\r\n\r\n`--with-openssl-opt=enable-tls1_3` is not necessary. \r\nThat is an OpenSSL parameter and does not work at BoringSSL.\r\n\r\n"
    },

      "body": "@xetorixik Excellent Patch! Problem solved. It seems that tls 1.3 draft 28 will be the final version and both openssl and boringssl are working on it and will be enabled by default in the future. "

      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "@JSkier21 @railjty Problem is that Google removed TLS 1.3 draft28 2 days ago (googlesource.com) and it seems logical that draft23 will follow soon in favor of TLS 1.3 RFC only. (Before draft 23,28 and RFC). \r\n\r\nAs Chrome and Firefox production version only supports TLS 1.3 draft and won't work yet on TLS 1.3 RFC. You will be faced with a choice in this interim phase.\r\n\r\nIn my opinion there are 3 options for now:\r\n\r\n1. Use for example BoringSSL git clone of Aug 25 2018 so the production version of both Chrome and Firefox are working fine with your BoringSSL draft/RFC based TLS 1.3 enabled site.\r\n\r\n2. Wait a little bit till [Chrome](https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=630147#c21) and [Firefox](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1057463) could offer support to TLS 1.3 RFC.\r\nAs could be seen above it is already available in the [Chromium master git](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src.git/+/f27cb7faf5b40e0c8b6f805bba47414da7ec4171%5E%21/). So this should not be long before it appears in the production version of Chrome.\r\n\r\n3. Don't do anything yet and jump in when everything is ready.\r\n"
    },

      "id": 417132964,
      "url": "https://github.com/cloudflare/sslconfig/issues/87#issuecomment-417132964",
      "created_at": "2018-08-29T22:53:23Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "@xetorixik, I just modified the 25 patch and defined tls13_all instead of _rfc. I now get final, draft 28, and draft 23 presented as options. Works great in Firefox and Chrome."
    },
    {
      "id": 417138868,
      "url": "https://github.com/cloudflare/sslconfig/issues/87#issuecomment-417138868",
      "created_at": "2018-08-29T23:21:31Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 7",
      "body": "@JSkier21 you mean you edited include/openssl/ssl.h for enum tls13_variant_t\r\n\r\nchanging\r\n\r\n```\r\ntls13_rfc = 0\r\n```\r\n\r\nto\r\n\r\n```\r\ntls13_all = 0\r\n```"
    },
    {
      "id": 417146807,
      "url": "https://github.com/cloudflare/sslconfig/issues/87#issuecomment-417146807",
      "created_at": "2018-08-30T00:03:09Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 7",
      "body": "seems i managed to re-enable all TLS 1.3 drafts via\r\n\r\n```\r\n        sed -i 's|tls13_rfc = 0|tls13_all = 0|' /opt/boringssl/include/openssl/ssl.h\r\n        sed -i 's|  tls13_all,|  tls13_rfc,|' /opt/boringssl/include/openssl/ssl.h\r\n        sed -i 's|tls13_variant_t tls13_variant = tls13_rfc;|tls13_variant_t tls13_variant = tls13_all;|g' /opt/boringssl/ssl/internal.h\r\n```\r\n\r\nbut wondering if i missed anything ?\r\n\r\ntestssl check\r\n\r\n```\r\n Testing protocols via sockets except NPN+ALPN \r\n\r\n SSLv2      not offered (OK)\r\n SSLv3      not offered (OK)\r\n TLS 1      offered\r\n TLS 1.1    offered\r\n TLS 1.2    offered (OK)\r\n TLS 1.3    offered (OK): draft 28, draft 23, final\r\n NPN/SPDY   not offered\r\n ALPN/HTTP2 h2, http/1.1 (offered)\r\n```"
    },

Should work fine with only you're last sed. Is there any reason why you're changing ssl.h file? I ask out of curiosity (maybe I'm missing something). "

    {
      "id": 417154538,

      "created_at": "2018-08-30T00:54:23Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-08-30T01:00:37Z",
      "author": "Participant 7",
      "body": "I am just winging it heh. Will try just editing internal.h only\r\n\r\nFYI i am not using boring patches as 1.15.3 enables tls 1.3 out of box with BoringSSL detected\r\n\r\nedit: yup confirmed editing internal.h only is enough to get all TLS 1.3 drafts re-enabled now\r\n\r\n```\r\nsed -i 's|tls13_variant_t tls13_variant = tls13_rfc;|tls13_variant_t tls13_variant = tls13_all;|g' /opt/boringssl/ssl/internal.h\r\n```"
